description: These files report how quickly Victoria's fire services reach emergencies, quarter by quarter, against their service delivery standards. The producer is the Country Fire Authority; an earlier metropolitan series came from the Metropolitan Fire Brigade and is listed alongside it. Coverage runs from the fourth quarter of 2016/17 to the second quarter of 2025/26 for the Country Fire Authority, and to the first quarter of 2019/20 for the Metropolitan Fire Brigade. Response time is measured from brigade alert to the first vehicle on scene and reported for each brigade area with at least ten emergency events, separately for each hazard class and its target; the metropolitan series uses station maintenance areas and targets of 7.7 minutes, or 9.2 minutes for emergency medical response. The files are available from the DataVic portal as quarterly XLSX downloads, free under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: small areas are omitted, files are spreadsheets with a layout that changes over time, and the metropolitan series stops at the first quarter of 2019/20. Simulation uses: calibrating travel and turnout times in fire service location models, measuring the effect of demand surges on response, and benchmarking emergency response resilience across areas. Related records: the San Francisco fire and EMS calls (data-sf-fire-ems-calls-for-service) give call-level response data for comparison.
